stories.title: RNA switch allows drug-controlled protein production
stories.summary: Bioengineers at the University of California San Diego have developed a technology that allows drugs to control when cells produce therapeutic proteins. The team claims this could make gene therapies safer and more adaptable for chronic diseases. The cells are now waiting for their instructions.

stories.title: Method identifies gut bacteria linked to inflammation
stories.summary: An international research team led by the University Hospital Tübingen and the University of Calgary has developed an approach to identify and selectively target gut bacteria that contribute to chronic inflammation. The method aims to enable personalized therapies for patients with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

stories.title: Microbe-made molecule heals gut lining
stories.summary: Scientists at Rutgers Health have discovered a molecule produced by gut bacteria that heals the intestinal lining. The team says the molecule protects against inflammatory diseases and triggers the production of a coenzyme that typically diminishes with age. The bacteria are doing the heavy lifting.

stories.title: Enzyme mapping provides clues for rare disease treatment
stories.summary: Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai have mapped an enzyme associated with glutaric aciduria type 1. The study reveals details about how the enzyme functions and is controlled, potentially offering a target for new treatments for the rare genetic disorder.

stories.title: Ovarian cancer study notes blood traces
stories.summary: High-grade serous ovarian cancer often begins in the fallopian tubes and is known for its rapid growth. New research is investigating whether early changes linked to this common cancer leave a detectable trace in the blood. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Trial results show survival in thymic tumor patients
stories.summary: Final results from the phase 2 PECATI clinical trial show long-term survival outcomes for patients with advanced B3-thymoma and thymic carcinoma. The treatment combined lenvatinib and pembrolizumab in patients who had previously received other therapies. The study provides data on the combination's performance.

stories.title: RNA therapy improves brain function in mice
stories.summary: Scientists at Johns Hopkins University and Academia Sinica have developed an experimental RNA-based treatment for brain receptor disorders. The therapy reportedly prevents brain damage and improves social behavior in mice with a genetic mutation linked to autism. The mice are showing improved memory.

stories.title: Hybrid therapy targets liver-dominant tumors
stories.summary: Combining intraarterial and intravenous administration of peptide receptor radionuclide therapy allows for intensified treatment of liver-dominant metastatic neuroendocrine tumors. The hybrid approach aims to deliver targeted care to the liver while maintaining systemic coverage. The method is described as safe.

stories.title: Researchers breed hybrid malaria parasite for vaccine
stories.summary: Researchers have created a hybrid malaria parasite combining the manufacturing ease of current vaccine strains with the high liver infectivity of a recent East African isolate. The work, published in JCI Insight, aims to build a more effective whole-parasite malaria vaccine.

stories.title: Long-term follow-up on heart stents
stories.summary: A 25-year follow-up study is examining whether heart stents prevent future heart attacks in stable patients. The research aims to provide new insight into the long-term efficacy of the procedure for this group. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Immune cells identified in insulin suppression
stories.summary: Researchers at IIT-Kanpur have identified a pathway where pancreatic macrophages rapidly suppress insulin release. The study suggests these cells can switch off insulin secretion within minutes. The team claims this opens a new avenue for protecting insulin production in patients with obesity and diabetes.

stories.title: Combination therapy reduces coronary plaque
stories.summary: A study suggests that rosuvastatin plus ezetimibe reduces coronary plaque volume more than atorvastatin alone. While the combination also lowered LDL cholesterol, researchers note that further study is required to determine if these plaque changes actually reduce the risk of future heart attacks or strokes.

stories.title: Regulator warns on anti-cancer drug prices
stories.summary: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs. The order capped trade margins at 30 percent. State drug controllers must submit action taken reports by November 16.

stories.title: New AIIMS record six crore consultations
stories.summary: The 22 new All India Institutes of Medical Sciences have recorded over six crore outpatient consultations since 2021. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare states that 18 of these institutions are now fully functional, providing emergency, trauma and inpatient services across the country.

stories.title: Women's Commission probes fertility center practices
stories.summary: The Telangana State Women's Commission has issued notices to eight fertility centers regarding an alleged illegal oocyte donation racket. The Commission initiated an inquiry into suspected irregularities in donor records. Several institutions were criticized for sending staff instead of senior management to the hearing.

stories.title: Domestic spending accounts for 86 percent of TB funding
stories.summary: The WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 states that domestic sources provided 86 percent of TB funding in 2025. International donor funding continues to fall, even as $22 billion is required annually to meet global targets. A quarter of all cases were concentrated in India.

stories.title: AIIMS begins pollution and lung cancer study
stories.summary: AIIMS has reportedly begun India's first study on the link between pollution and lung cancer as air quality in Delhi declines. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: NHA to restrict Ayushman Bharat treatments
stories.summary: The National Health Authority is reportedly moving to restrict 112 treatments under the Ayushman Bharat scheme to government hospitals. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Air pollution and health in India: A review of epidemiological evidence to Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air
stories.summary: Air pollution is no longer just an environmental concern in India, it is a primary determinant of public health, as millions face chronic exposure outdoors, at home, and at work. stories.title: India reports 38 percent drop in TB mortality
stories.summary: India reduced tuberculosis mortality by 38 percent since 2015, outpacing the global decline of 35 percent, according to the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026. The Health Ministry also reported a 94 percent treatment success rate for drug-susceptible cases. The ministry says the data is now official.

stories.title: Why West Bengal’s C-Sections, at nearly 1 in 2 births, demand a hard look
stories.summary: On September 29, 2015, a memo went out from Swasthya Bhawan, the West Bengal Health Department’s headquarters in Salt Lake, to every medical college principal and every district’s chief medical officer of health. Its subject was a concern the Union Health Ministry had raised about

stories.title: India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report
stories.summary: India has seen a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, compared to a global average of 35%, and a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB, according to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026. stories.title: Karnataka to track used cooking oil with new app
stories.summary: Karnataka is developing a mobile application to track the collection and sale of used cooking oil. The initiative aims to prevent the oil from re-entering the food chain by creating a digital trail from purchase to industrial disposal. The app is expected within three months.

stories.title: Experts urge coordinated action on antimicrobial resistance
stories.summary: Antimicrobial resistance was associated with over 4.7 million deaths in 2021, according to experts at the Global Media Forum on AMR. Officials cited gaps in financing and surveillance as primary obstacles to progress. Global commitments are now being asked to translate into results on the ground.

stories.title: BIMSTEC ministers adopt regional public health plan
stories.summary: Health ministers from seven Bay of Bengal countries have adopted a revised public health action plan for 2026 to 2030. The agreement covers disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, and digital health. The meeting in Colombo focused on shared priorities for regional health security and workforce development.

stories.title: Florida records highest dengue outbreak in decades
stories.summary: Florida has recorded 524 locally acquired cases of dengue fever as of October 31, the highest number since the disease returned to the state in 2009. While most infections cause mild symptoms, at least one person has died. Officials expect the disease to become more common.

stories.title: California beach closed following E. coli outbreak
stories.summary: Santa Cruz County officials closed Capitola Beach after at least nine children became ill with E. coli infections. Authorities are currently testing local water sources, including the ocean and nearby lagoons, to identify the source of the contamination. Visitors have been urged to avoid the water.

stories.title: India and Bangladesh ban paraquat to aid suicide prevention
stories.summary: Bangladesh and India have banned paraquat, an acutely toxic pesticide linked to one in five global suicides. The chemical is also associated with neurological risks for agricultural workers and children. The move is intended to prevent ingestion-related deaths and protect brain health in rural communities.

stories.title: Zus Health raises $33 million for data platform
stories.summary: Zus Health raised $33 million in Series B funding to unify fragmented clinical information from pharmacies and laboratories. The platform uses AI to generate patient summaries for clinicians. CEO Jonathan Bush says the company aims to move beyond the current silos of electronic medical records.

stories.title: Ukraine health ministry drafts AI rules
stories.summary: Ukraine's Health Ministry is drafting legislation to govern medical AI systems, citing risks and safety concerns. The move follows a survey finding that 80.5% of Ukrainian clinicians already use AI in their work. The ministry is now attempting to catch up with the workplace.

stories.title: CHIME releases digital health trends report
stories.summary: The College of Healthcare Information Management Executives has published its 2026 Digital Health Most Wired National Trends Report. The document provides an in-depth view of the technologies and leadership practices currently shaping digital health across the United States. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Happiest Health launches digital business
stories.summary: Wellness enterprise Happiest Health has launched a digital business vertical, pledging to invest INR 500 Cr in technology over five years. Half of the funds are earmarked for digital health, with 11 applications planned for release within 18 months. The company is currently building its portfolio.

stories.title: EkaCare to provide AI scribes for public health
stories.summary: The National Health Authority has selected EkaCare as a technology partner for its ambient AI voice scribe solution. The project, intended for doctors in public health organizations, will run on Amazon Web Services infrastructure. The agency chose the firm through an expression of interest process.

stories.title: Pocket ECG device reaches 60,000 units
stories.summary: Sunfox Technologies has deployed over 60,000 units of Spandan, a pocket-sized ECG device that connects to smartphones. The founders developed the tool to bypass the need for conventional machines or internet access in remote areas. It provides a medical-grade report in minutes.

stories.title: Digital adoption linked to rural health outcomes
stories.summary: A study of rural households in South India found that those using digital technologies reported better personal health than non-adopting neighbors. Published in Discover Public Health, the research used ordinal logistic regression to analyze data from 2,872 households. Technology appears to correlate with self-rated well-being.

stories.title: FDA receives 540 comments on AI regulation
stories.summary: The FDA received 540 submissions regarding its proposed regulatory framework for generative AI in medical devices. Industry groups are calling for regulatory flexibility, while patient advocates demand stronger clinical evidence and oversight. The agency is currently reviewing the divide between the two groups.

stories.title: Medicare AI experiment faces scrutiny
stories.summary: New documents have raised questions regarding Medicare's prior-authorization experiment involving artificial intelligence. The program, which uses automated systems to approve or deny medical procedures, remains a focal point for those tracking how technology is integrated into clinical care. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: EkaCare deploys voice scribe for doctors
stories.summary: EkaCare is deploying an ambient AI voice scribe for public healthcare doctors under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. The system uses the company's proprietary speech model to convert patient conversations into structured digital records. The goal is to reduce the time spent on clinical documentation.

stories.title: Israel digital health model gains attention
stories.summary: Israel's digitized health system is being discussed in American policy circles as a contrast to the fragmented U.S. model. While Israeli doctors can access a patient's full medical history instantly, American patients often struggle to transfer records. The system's efficiency remains a point of envy.

stories.title: Akara raises $5.5 million for hospital AI
stories.summary: Akara has raised $5.5 million in new funding, bringing its total capital to $12.3 million. The company develops sensors and robotics intended to reduce administrative burdens and coordinate hospital services. It claims its technology helps hospitals treat more patients with privacy-preserving AI.

stories.title: FIU professor discusses immigration and mental health
stories.summary: Dr. Eugenio M. Rothe presented 40 years of research on the mental health impacts of immigration at Florida International University. He noted that 30% of the university's students are first-generation graduates. The presentation focused on the challenges faced by immigrants and refugees in the United States.

stories.title: Researcher honored for mental health tools
stories.summary: Dr. Amir Khajavinia has received the Governor General's Gold Medal at the University of Saskatchewan. The award recognizes his academic record and his work developing measurement tools for psychedelic compound research. His efforts aim to advance the scientific understanding of mental health treatments.

stories.title: BRICS nations discuss child mental health
stories.summary: Experts from five nations met at AIIMS Delhi to discuss child mental health and the removal of social stigma. Participants highlighted the need for early identification in schools and community support. They noted that fear and misconceptions often prove more obstructive than the conditions themselves.

stories.title: Global study finds mental health workforce gaps
stories.summary: A global analysis has identified a geographic mismatch between youth mental health burdens and the availability of professional practitioners. Researchers examined data for individuals aged 10 to 24 across various jurisdictions. The study highlights regions where high healthcare needs coincide with low practitioner density.

stories.title: Bromfield survey shows mental health trends
stories.summary: A survey of 384 students at Bromfield School found improvements in mental health and a decline in risky behaviors. Administered by Market Street Research, the study reached 79% of the student body. School committee members reviewed the findings, which included both encouraging results and some concerns.

stories.title: Conference calls for mental health stigma reduction
stories.summary: The 11th Together Against Stigma Conference is underway at AIIMS New Delhi. Organized by The George Institute and UNICEF India, the event brings together experts and advocates to discuss improving access to care. The three-day meeting focuses on five priorities for reducing mental health discrimination.

stories.title: Study analyzes youth mental health on social media
stories.summary: Researchers analyzed 957 posts and 763 comments on Reddit and TikTok to understand how young people disclose mental health challenges online. Published in Discover Mental Health, the study investigated the motivations behind these disclosures and how other users respond. The internet is now a primary coping mechanism.

stories.title: Digital mental health platform sees high satisfaction but low uptake
stories.summary: A three-year study of the enhance platform across six German universities found exceptionally high student satisfaction and well-being gains. However, only 117 of the 447 students who completed baseline assessments attended at least one individual counselling session. Satisfaction is apparently easier to achieve than attendance.

stories.title: Smartphone game shows promise as antidepressant add-on
stories.summary: A randomized controlled trial in Sweden found that a smartphone game, combined with therapy modules, reduced depression and anxiety symptoms for adults already taking antidepressants. While participants reported better medication adherence, their quality of life did not differ from those on a waitlist. Games are not life.

stories.title: Research suggests youth incarceration harms mental health
stories.summary: Researchers and advocates argue that detaining youth leads to new or worsened mental health conditions, including depression and suicidality. The study notes that incarceration often results in deeper criminal legal system involvement in adulthood, while failing to make communities any safer. The system was designed for protection.

stories.title: Weekly park visits linked to better child mental health
stories.summary: University of Exeter researchers analysed data from 4,219 children and found those visiting a park at least once a week showed better social-emotional development. The study suggests that communities require high-quality parks that are safe and accessible. The outdoors remains a recommended location for development.

stories.title: Mental health app helps unemployed find work
stories.summary: A Northwestern University study found that 68.3 percent of participants using the DRIVEN smartphone programme found jobs after six weeks, compared to 50.8 percent receiving traditional guidance. The programme combines mental health exercises with job-search support. Stress is now being managed by an acronym.

research.title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent
research.summary: A new study reveals that viral infections may leave behind hidden damage to the immune system long after symptoms disappear. Researchers found that mice recovering from an acute infection experienced lasting changes to their spleens and weakened immune responses, potentially leaving them more vulnerable to future threats. research.title: Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch
research.summary: A major study of nearly 1,900 older adults suggests that stopping statins after age 70 may be relatively safe in the short term for people who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke. However, a higher rate of serious cardiovascular events or death during longer follow-up raises.

research.title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
research.summary: A study of more than 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications when used for weight loss, but was associated with a higher risk of premature birth when prescribed for diabetes. research.title: Vaccines could be a new frontier in KRAS targeting
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 13 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04772-1 A convergence of therapeutic and technological advances reveals KRAS-targeting vaccination as a potential new approach to preventing the recurrence of pancreatic cancer, but many hurdles remain.

research.title: Colorectal cancer is rising again after 20 years, and scientists don't know why
research.summary: Colorectal cancer is making an alarming comeback in the United States after more than 20 years of declining rates, and the increase is no longer limited to younger adults.
